rules.title: Standard port group rejects promiscuous mode (effective policy)
rules.rationale: Promiscuous mode lets a VM capture traffic of every VM on the port group.

mitigation.summary: Set promiscuous mode to Reject on the port group and its vSwitch.
steps: Host > Networking > Port group > Edit > Security

rules.title: Standard port group rejects MAC address changes (effective policy)
rules.rationale: Accepting MAC changes enables impersonation of other hosts.

mitigation.summary: Set MAC address changes to Reject.
steps: Host > Networking > Port group > Edit > Security

rules.title: Standard port group rejects forged transmits (effective policy)
rules.rationale: Forged transmits allow spoofed source MAC addresses.

steps: Host > Networking > Port group > Edit > Security

rules.title: Standard vSwitch default security policy rejects all three
rules.rationale: New port groups inherit the vSwitch default.

mitigation.summary: Set the vSwitch security policy to Reject for all three settings.

rules.title: Distributed port group rejects promiscuous mode
rules.rationale: Promiscuous mode lets a VM capture traffic of other VMs.

mitigation.summary: Set promiscuous mode to Reject on the distributed port group.

rules.title: Distributed port group rejects MAC address changes

mitigation.summary: Set MAC address changes to Reject.

rules.title: Distributed port group rejects forged transmits
rules.rationale: Forged transmits allow spoofed source MAC addresses.

rules.title: Port-level security policy overrides are not allowed
rules.rationale: Allowing overrides lets individual ports diverge from the reviewed portgroup policy.

mitigation.summary: Disable security policy override on the distributed port group.
steps: dvPortgroup > Edit Settings > Advanced > Override port policies

rules.title: No individual ports accept promiscuous, MAC change or forged transmits
rules.rationale: Effective per-port settings matter; a portgroup default does not prove every port is compliant.

mitigation.summary: Reset permissive port overrides and disable override permission.
steps: dvSwitch > Ports > Edit settings for affected ports

rules.title: Distributed switch default security policy rejects all three
rules.rationale: New distributed port groups inherit the switch default.

mitigation.summary: Set the VDS default port security policy to Reject for all three.

rules.title: Port groups do not use VLAN 4095 (trunk to guest) without authorization
rules.rationale: VLAN 4095 passes all VLANs to the guest (VGT) and should be limited to approved appliances.

mitigation.summary: Assign a specific VLAN, or record an exception for approved VGT appliances.

rules.title: Port groups do not use the upstream native VLAN
rules.rationale: Traffic on the native VLAN is untagged upstream and can be used for VLAN hopping.

mitigation.summary: Move port groups off the native VLAN.

rules.limitations: Requires the native VLAN from the scope file or CDP/LLDP evidence; otherwise UNKNOWN (1.x assumed VLAN 1).

rules.title: Port groups do not use VLANs reserved by upstream switches
rules.rationale: Reserved VLANs on common switch platforms can cause traffic to be dropped or mishandled.

mitigation.summary: Use VLANs outside the switch vendor's reserved ranges.

rules.limitations: Reserved ranges are vendor-specific; defaults reflect common Cisco platforms.

rules.title: NetFlow/IPFIX is exported only to authorized collectors
rules.rationale: Flow exports reveal traffic patterns of all workloads.

mitigation.summary: Point IPFIX to an authorized collector or disable it.

rules.title: VDS health check is disabled
rules.rationale: Health check frames disclose VLAN and MTU configuration to the physical network.

mitigation.summary: Disable VLAN/MTU and teaming health checks when not troubleshooting.

rules.title: Port mirroring sessions are authorized

check.guidance: Confirm every mirroring session and destination is approved

rules.rationale: Mirroring copies workload traffic to another port or remote destination.

rules.title: Virtual switch has redundant physical uplinks
rules.rationale: A single uplink is a single point of failure for every workload on the switch.

mitigation.summary: Add a second uplink on a separate physical switch.
steps: Host > Networking > vSwitch > Manage physical adapters
